elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: The added clause permits Customer to terminate “this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience.”

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Termination is permitted upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Vendor must refund prepaid Fees pro rata for the period after the effective termination date.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that Vendor has no convenience-termination right during a committed term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The operative notice period is thirty days, not 60 to 90 days.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed, so the conditional cap requirement is satisfied.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: No Vendor convenience-termination right is granted, and Vendor is expressly barred from such termination during a committed term; this is more restrictive than an end-of-term-only right.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No Vendor convenience-termination right is granted, so the notice condition cannot arise.
